heading: Make the likelihood estimate and control decision auditable
paragraphs: A probability needs an event definition and a time unit. In this original example, interpret 15% as the assumed chance of at least one specified supplier interruption during the next quarter, with $16,000 as the modeled loss if it occurs. This is a deliberately simplified single-event model. A recurring incident count requires a frequency model instead; do not multiply a probability of at least one event by an assumed number of incidents without explaining the change.

The December 2025 NIST risk-estimation revision addresses cybersecurity risk, while the Canadian public-service register illustrates context, controls, residual exposure and ownership. Neither supplies this workshop’s probabilities. Record the evidence behind the original estimate and the assumptions behind the proposed 8% residual estimate. Until the backup supplier passes its qualification test, retain the uncontrolled scenario in the decision record.

For a fair comparison, charge the $600 control cost against the same quarter used for the $1,120 modeled exposure reduction. If the $600 is one-time setup but benefits last longer, build a multi-period comparison rather than repeating or omitting the setup arbitrarily. Also test the cost on the actual payment date: a control can improve a probability-weighted comparison while worsening this week’s cash low point. Approval should state who accepts the remaining exposure, what evidence would invalidate the estimate and which trigger starts the contingency action.

faq.q: Is the 15% probability a published industry rate?
faq.a: No. It is a fictional quarterly assumption used to explain the method. A real assessment needs dated evidence and an explicit event definition.

faq.q: Can a one-time control cost be compared with an annual benefit directly?
faq.a: First align the time horizon. Record setup and recurring costs separately and model benefits over the same periods.

heading: Test the rights, dependency and cash behind the offer
paragraphs: Before paying for a supposedly automated store or template package, identify exactly what you will own or be permitted to use: the domain, customer relationship, source files, product images, software account and supplier arrangement. Record restrictions on commercial use and resale. An attractive mockup does not establish that the seller owns the materials or that a marketplace will permit the proposed activity.

The FTC’s business-opportunity warning describes the danger of unsupported online-store earnings promises. Treat projected revenue as an assumption until supported by records that also show costs and unsuccessful outcomes. Check the seller, cancellation terms, references and any applicable disclosure obligations before buying an opportunity. A third-party service’s claim is not evidence that your own account, inventory or delivery system can achieve its result.

Use the existing original ecommerce case to separate unsold stock from lost cash. Paying $2,100 for fifty units and selling thirty leaves twenty units costing $840 in the simplified stock record. Cash has already left for all fifty, but that does not make the remaining twenty units another acquisition expense for each of the thirty sold. Investigate damage or unsellability separately. For a digital download, retain a dated version and test the file in the promised application; for the service, log revisions and unpaid selling time. The next decision is whether repeat orders remain deliverable at the recorded net economics, not whether the model can be described as passive income.

faq.q: Does an automated-store provider guarantee a usable business?
faq.a: No. Verify account control, permitted activity, delivery responsibilities, total costs and the evidence behind earnings claims.

faq.q: Are the twenty unsold units automatically a loss?
faq.a: Not in this simplified inventory example. They remain stock subject to the applicable measurement assessment, although their purchase has already used cash.

heading: Set separate launch tests for merchandise and service promises
paragraphs: For US merchandise covered by the FTC’s order rule guidance, a seller needs a reasonable basis for its stated shipping time; when no shipping time is stated, the usual rule is shipment within thirty days after a properly completed order. If timely shipment becomes impossible, follow the applicable delay-consent or cancellation/refund procedure. This is not a universal thirty-day delivery rule for every online transaction, and the FTC guidance identifies exemptions and special cases. Services are outside this merchandise rule.

For the original service pilot, make the delivery promise testable: what file or work product is due, how the buyer confirms receipt, which revisions are included and who handles a failed handoff. A payment receipt establishes a payment event; it does not by itself prove completed service performance. Keep the five fictional orders labeled as teaching data when presenting the 25% inquiry conversion. Replace them with dated, consented business records before describing a real customer result.

The launch decision should have separate evidence for offer accuracy, payment, fulfillment and customer communications. The FTC review-rule Q&A explains why businesses must avoid fake or false testimonials and incentives conditioned on a particular review sentiment. Ask genuine buyers for their actual experience; a test order, generated persona or fictional worked case must not become a customer endorsement. Record unresolved launch defects with an owner and retest the repaired step before increasing demand.

faq.q: Does the FTC’s usual thirty-day shipping rule cover my consulting service?
faq.a: The cited rule concerns covered merchandise orders, not services. Service promises still need their own applicable contractual and legal assessment.

faq.q: Can the fictional five-order pilot be described as a client result?
faq.a: No. It is a teaching example. Actual result claims need genuine underlying records and an accurate description of what was measured.

replacements.from: Five divided by twenty is a 25% conversion for this tiny observed pilot
replacements.to: Five divided by twenty is a 25% conversion for this fictional teaching pilot

heading: Separate premises permission, tax treatment and usable capacity
paragraphs: Keep three decisions in different records: permission to conduct the activity at the address, the cash required to operate it, and any tax deduction. The SBA location guidance notes that zoning can apply to home businesses; the Arizona source is only an example for that jurisdiction. A permitted home activity does not automatically qualify its owner for a federal home-office deduction, and a possible deduction does not create local operating permission.

IRS Topic 509 describes qualifying business uses and the exclusive-and-regular-use tests that apply to many home-office claims, with specific exceptions such as qualifying storage and daycare. Do not infer a deduction merely from calling a room an office or allocating household rent in a planning budget. Preserve the relevant use records and review the actual tax requirements separately from this original operating case.

In the fictional capacity case, twenty jobs need forty delivery hours, leaving none of that delivery allowance unused. The sixteen hours already reserved for administration and selling must not be counted again as spare delivery capacity. Log actual booked time, completed jobs, cancellations and rework for the same month. If a job needs 2.5 hours, the sixteen-job ceiling leaves only $1,170 after the stated $350 commitments. Changing tax assumptions cannot repair that physical capacity shortfall. Revisit price, scope, scheduling or the owner-income target using evidence from completed work before accepting a fully loaded calendar.

faq.q: Does permission to work from home establish a tax deduction?
faq.a: No. Local operating permission and federal tax qualification are separate questions.

faq.q: Are the sixteen administration hours spare delivery capacity?
faq.a: No. They are already reserved in this example. Using them for jobs would require a revised plan for the administration and selling work.

heading: Trace a real document through all four financial statements
paragraphs: The SEC’s financial-statement primer distinguishes a reporting-date balance sheet from statements covering a period. Use that distinction when explaining the original eight transactions: the $6,000 borrowing belongs in the liability balance and cash movement, not in sales. The $2,500 customer collection reduces an existing receivable without adding another $2,500 of earned income. The identity of the bank transaction is insufficient without its source document.

For each actual entry, retain the date, economic event, supporting document, debit, credit and reviewer. OpenStax’s transaction-analysis lesson shows how supported events affect the equation. The article’s owner-investment and withdrawal labels describe a simplified owner-equity case; a corporation would normally use its own share-capital, retained-earnings and distribution accounts. Changing the entity’s account labels does not authorize classifying a dividend as wages or a loan as revenue.

A useful final check is to explain the difference between $2,800 included profit and $20,000 closing cash without a plug. Owner investment contributes $18,000; the loan contributes $6,000; equipment acquisition uses $5,000; part of earned revenue remains in the $1,500 receivable; $500 of expense remains unpaid; and the owner withdraws $800. Each belongs in its own bridge. A proposed market sale price or an estimate of employee expertise must not be inserted into the balance sheet simply to increase equity. Recognition and measurement require the applicable accounting policy, not an attractive valuation story.

faq.q: Why are the closing cash balance and included profit different?
faq.a: Investment, financing, asset purchases, unpaid customer and supplier balances, and withdrawals affect cash and equity differently.

faq.q: Can a corporation reuse the owner-equity labels unchanged?
faq.a: Use accounts appropriate to the legal entity and reporting framework. Share capital, retained earnings and distributions require their own supported records.

heading: Document the reporting basis before interpreting the subtotal
paragraphs: This is a classified-balance-sheet teaching case for a US business with a short operating cycle, not a complete rulebook for every reporting framework. OpenStax’s classification lesson explains the introductory one-year-or-longer-operating-cycle boundary. A maturity date alone is insufficient for every unusual asset: document the asset’s purpose, restriction, expected realization or consumption and the applicable policy. Do not take an issuer’s taxonomy label in a filing as the accounting standard itself.

Create a review line for each original balance. The $9,000 gross receivable needs invoice and settlement support; the $600 allowance needs a separate estimate; $7,000 inventory needs count, cost and condition evidence; $1,200 prepaid insurance needs the unconsumed coverage schedule. These records support different judgments. A current classification does not validate the amount, and a supported carrying amount does not establish that the item can pay tomorrow’s bill. Reconcile the net $8,400 receivable once rather than adding its gross and net presentations.

For the $2,000 deposit excluded from current assets, the example assumes a genuine long-term restriction consistent with the stated reporting policy, rather than merely an account named restricted cash. Confirm the contract, permitted withdrawals and release conditions. If those facts change, reassess classification before recalculating the subtotal; do not change a label only to improve working capital. Preserve current and noncurrent portions where the policy requires them. Use the same reporting date and accounting basis for the liability comparison, then build a separate collection and payment calendar from actual expected dates.

faq.q: Is a taxonomy description in a company filing the accounting standard?
faq.a: No. It is a filing-related label or definition, and its presence on a regulator’s site does not make it regulator-authored accounting guidance.

faq.q: Does a current label validate the carrying amount?
faq.a: No. Classification and measurement require different evidence, such as dates and restrictions versus valuation and recoverability.

replacements.to: • OpenStax: introductory current-asset classification and liquidity; not an accounting standard

heading: Separate the recognized balance, debt terms and settlement plan
paragraphs: This original schedule is an introductory classified-balance-sheet case for a short-cycle US business. OpenStax’s current-liability lesson supports the listed common categories. Do not extend the simplified $3,000-current/$9,000-noncurrent loan split to a loan with different terms. Read contractual maturities, demand clauses, covenant compliance and relevant refinancing evidence under the applicable reporting framework before assigning the portions. A lender’s informal expectation of renewal is not the same evidence as an executed right or agreement.

Build a debt register with opening principal, new borrowings, principal repaid, closing principal, interest, next payment and classification assessment. Interest and principal answer different questions. The $250 principal payment in the original thirty-day schedule does not assert that no interest will be paid; the $9,750 total includes only the listed items. Add any actual interest and other omitted commitments to the separate cash plan without quietly changing the supported accounting balances.

For customer advances, reconcile opening liability plus new receipts less amounts earned, approved refunds and other supported movements. The $2,000 advance in this case remains a service obligation at cutoff; it is not assumed to require an immediate $2,000 cash repayment. Its fulfillment can still require future payroll or supplies, so excluding that automatic refund is not permission to exclude delivery cash. Record refund conditions and delivery evidence. The classification schedule, the expense budget and the dated cash forecast should reconcile through explained differences rather than being forced into one identical total.

faq.q: Does the $9,750 cash illustration include every future payment?
faq.a: No. It totals only the listed near-term items. Actual interest, delivery costs and other commitments need separate dated entries.

faq.q: Can an expected loan renewal determine classification by itself?
faq.a: No. Review the actual rights, agreements, timing and applicable reporting rules rather than relying on an informal expectation.

replacements.to: • OpenStax: current-liability recognition and reporting examples; not an accounting standard

heading: Resolve unapplied cash and report exceptions without hiding balances
paragraphs: Run three linked but separate records: the invoice and credit ledger, the receipt-allocation record, and the bank reconciliation. Microsoft’s receivables process documentation separates invoices, credits, customer payments, prepayments, refunds and settlement. It describes a product workflow rather than prescribing a universal accounting policy. Your control record should still explain which event occurred, who approved it and how it links to the customer balance.

For a separate original receipt example, a customer sends $1,200 against a supported $1,000 invoice. Apply $1,000 to that invoice and investigate the remaining $200 using remittance evidence. Do not increase revenue or create a second invoice merely to absorb the receipt. The balance may be an advance, an overpayment awaiting refund or another supported item; decide from the facts and accounting policy. Preserve both the gross bank receipt and its allocations so the customer account does not appear settled through an unexplained journal.

At review, list outstanding disputes, unallocated receipts, approved-but-unposted credits and promised payments with owner and next action. Reconcile those exceptions to the same cutoff as the $8,500 gross ledger. Keep any allowance assessment separate from cash collection; the OpenStax receivable examples distinguish earned sales from later settlement. A write-off or allowance change can alter a reported balance without collecting cash. Collection speed should not be improved cosmetically by changing due dates, netting unrelated parties or silently removing disputed invoices.

faq.q: How should a receipt larger than the invoice be handled?
faq.a: Allocate the supported invoice amount and investigate the excess using remittance evidence. Do not invent sales to absorb the difference.

faq.q: Can gross receivables and the bank balance happen to be equal?
faq.a: Yes, numerically by coincidence. They represent different accounts and are reconciled to different supporting records.

replacements.from: An AR ledger cannot equal the bank balance because it represents unpaid amounts rather than cash held.
replacements.to: The AR control balance is not expected to reconcile to the bank balance: it represents unpaid customer amounts, while the bank balance represents cash held.

replacements.from: JPMorgan’s receivables guidance describes the broad sequence from credit assessment through cash application and reconciliation.
replacements.to: Microsoft’s receivables process documentation distinguishes invoicing, customer payments, credits and settlement.

heading: Keep matching tolerance and payment authority separate
paragraphs: Microsoft’s matching documentation distinguishes two-way price checks from three-way checks that also compare receipt quantities. In the original case, ninety accepted units at $20 support $1,800 of received goods, while the $2,000 invoice contains a $200 quantity exception. A system tolerance is a configured review threshold, not proof that an incorrect invoice is economically correct or that missing goods arrived.

Retain the original invoice, receiving record, exception decision and supplier correction. SAP’s reconciliation example illustrates keeping the original document and the reconciliation trail separately. A documented partial payment, credit or corrected invoice must explain its effect on the remaining supplier balance. Resolving a matching icon does not itself show that a bank payment was authorized or settled; those events need their own references.

Protect supplier-master changes as a separate control. The FBI’s IC3 guidance recommends verifying account-change requests through another channel. For an actual payment run, confirm changed bank details through a previously trusted contact route, retain the verification and review the payee independently of invoice approval. If only one person operates the business, keep a visible callback and approval record rather than treating the sender’s email as confirmation. After settlement, allocate the receipt or payment reference to the invoice, reconcile the resulting $6,200 example balance, and investigate any unexplained supplier-statement difference before closing the period.

faq.q: Does an allowed matching tolerance prove the invoice is correct?
faq.a: No. It is a configured control threshold. The underlying purchase, receipt and supplier evidence still determine the supported amount.

faq.q: Does invoice approval also approve a changed bank account?
faq.a: Treat bank-detail verification as a separate control using a trusted independent contact route.
